given: a stock record already exists for a (sku, location) pair
when: a team member files that same (sku, location) pair again with a new quantity and tracking code
then: exactly one record exists for that pair, holding the newly filed values, with no second record stored for the pair

independence.rationale: AC1 and AC2 cover a first-time filing and its read-back; this AC observes collision resolution at write time (single record, no duplicate), which can break by storing two records while first-time filing still works.

architectural_notes: E2E: observes write-time collision resolution end to end. The service (app/services/) implements create-or-update on the (sku, location) key (last-write-wins upsert), backed by the DB composite unique constraint PI1 on stock_records so exactly one row survives even under a race; the repository (app/repositories/) is the only layer issuing the ORM upsert. Cross-cutting: the (sku, location) uniqueness invariant (R3) is owned jointly by the service upsert logic and the DB unique constraint, never in the boundary; the transaction boundary sits in the service, never the domain/model. Verified as a real integration test against the paired Lakebase branch (refile same pair, assert single row holds the new values).
